name: memU (v2, memu-cli)
repo: https://github.com/NevaMind-AI/memU (also https://github.com/NevaMind-AI/memU-experiment @ f178ce9 for the v1 LoCoMo run; tag v1.2.0 @ a4cff91 read for the v1 library)
one_line: Memory as agent-written markdown files: a scheduled job hands new host-agent transcripts back to the host agent itself to patch memory/skill files, and an LLM-free engine only embeds one segment per line and returns cosine top-5 segments plus file paths.

locomo.protocol: memU-experiment harness (v1 code, not HEAD): gpt-4.1-mini reader (Azure deployment 'gpt-4.1-mini-2'), gpt-4.1 yes/no judge, use_profile=prompt (whole character profile file injected into the answer prompt), up to 3 retrieve/sufficiency iterations; 1,420/1,542 q = cat 1-4 (1,540) + the only 2 cat-5 items that carry an 'answer' field (444 cat-5 items skipped for missing 'answer'); memory store pre-built in an unreleased dir 'memory_0721_4_1_with_profile' (272/272 sessions skipped at run time, build model not recorded)

Absent from HEAD README; MemU is not in OmniMemEval, JustMem or T-Mem (memspine/evals/analysis/SOTA_MEMU_MEMOS_LOCOMO.md section 11)

arch.product.t: Sidecar CLI for desktop coding agents (Codex, Claude Code plus Claude Cowork audit logs through the Claude Code bridge, Cursor, OpenClaw, Hermes, WorkBuddy, Cola, pi, generic memu-agent), a developer 'memu memorize prepare/commit' path for 1-10 supplied sessions, a Python library and a hosted cloud backend (api.memu.so); README claims 'core memory logic is only 500 lines'. The engine itself is embedding-only: 'No LLM is involved anywhere'.
arch.product.e: read: src/memu/app/service.py:24-32, src/memu/cli.py:310-311, src/memu/hosts/cowork/sessions.py:1-17, src/memu/cloud.py:13; doc: README.md:23, :114-131, docs/adr/0018-cowork-through-claude-code-bridge.md

arch.truth.t: The configured backend store (RecallFile rows) is authoritative. Bridging works on writable per-host mirrors at ~/.memu/hosts/<host>/{memory,skill} (Codex keeps the older ~/.memu root), rewritten page by page from the store at every prepare; the retrieve hook separately writes ~/.memu/<track>/<name>.md for each hit file so it can hand the agent a path.

arch.stores.t: Three tables only: Resource (touched workspace file path + caption + embedding), RecallFile (name, track memory|skill, description, content, file embedding), RecallFileSegment (one text line + embedding + denormalised track, FK to file). Backends: inmemory (library default), SQLite (memu CLI default ./data/memu.sqlite3; MEMU_DB is required for host adapters), Postgres+pgvector (schema via Alembic).

arch.graphdb.t: No graph. ADR 0007 explicitly drops graph, entity index and multi-hop: 'no graph layer and no external database'.

arch.scope.t: Pluggable user scope model, default fields user_id and agent_id, applied as where filters with a non-unique scope index. No unique database index on file names: the SQLite tables and the Alembic Postgres schema declare none (the unused Postgres ORM model would cover name+scope without track); (name, track, scope) uniqueness is enforced in code by get-or-create lookup and commit-plan dedupe. Host adapters call retrieve and commit with no where, so a local install is one shared store across all hosts. Cloud accepts only exact user_id/agent_id.

write.entry.t: commit_results(recall_files=[{name, track, description, content}], resource=[{path, description}]); reached through '<host> prepare' then agent work then '<host> commit' (bridging), or 'memu memorize prepare/commit' for 1-10 developer sessions.

write.receipt.t: Synchronous and durable when commit returns: plan, then a single embed() call for every new text (sent as sequential requests of up to 64 texts over one HTTP connection, each retried up to 3 times on 408/429/5xx), then writes; an embedding failure writes nothing so the commit can be retried whole. The session cursor and file snapshot advance only after the store accepts (#518). Storage failures mid-write are not rolled back.

write.roles.t: Memory jobs see user and assistant messages only; skill jobs see messages plus tool calls and results. Host adapters drop thinking blocks, meta-injected records and (Codex) user-role harness injections such as <environment_context> and AGENTS.md text.

write.firewall.t: No injection or poisoning defence on content. The only filter is structural (drop harness-injected records, drop the bridging run's own sessions, ADR 0015). The agent writes whatever it judges durable.

write.governance.t: Adapters strip runtime metadata fields (cwd, gitBranch, sessionId, timestamp, usage) before transcripts reach the agent; no PII/secret redaction, no consent or retention policy. Uninstall keeps the store unless the user asks to erase it.

segment.unit.t: One host session's new records since the last cursor = one memory job + one skill job (agent passes, not single LLM calls); at most 10 sessions per run (MAX_JOBS = 10, --max-jobs), plus one resource-describe job per run only when at least one session was prepared.

segment.rule.t: Boundary = host session file plus a per-host cursor (line count, or line count plus rewrite generation for OpenClaw SQLite) promoted only on commit; scan newest-first and stop a scan region at the first unchanged seen session; sessions whose new records are all noise are marked seen without using a job slot. No topic or time segmentation inside a session.

segment.measured.t: Not measured; HEAD has no LoCoMo harness. v1 experiment used LoCoMo's 272 sessions as given.

extract.calls.t: Engine: 0 LLM calls (embeddings only). Distillation is delegated to the host agent: per session one memory job and one skill job (each a multi-step agentic run with bash reads), plus one resource job per run; scheduled every 60 min by default.

extract.facts.t: No atomic fact records. The agent writes or patches topic-level markdown memory files (front-matter name + one-line description + body); every non-blank, non-heading body line becomes one embedded segment, deduplicated within the file.

extract.episode.t: No episode narratives; the memory prompt targets 'stable facts about the user, their projects, and how they like to work'.

extract.dates.t: Not requested by the memory prompt, and adapters delete the timestamp field from Claude Code and Codex records before the agent sees them, so dates rarely reach memory text. (v1 experiment prefixed every event with 'Mentioned at {session_date}:'.)

extract.neighbours.t: Each job points the agent at the mirrored existing memory/skill directory; it reads file names first and only opens bodies that look related, then chooses no-op, patch in place, or create.

extract.failure.t: Fail-safe by staging: prepare writes only a pending cursor; a run that dies before commit leaves cursor and content-hash snapshot unchanged, so the sessions are re-offered next run (bounded re-work). Job templates fall back server -> last-good cache -> embedded.

graph.entities.t: not found; ADR 0007 rejects an entity layer.

graph.resolution.t: not found (only file-name keying within a track).

graph.communities.t: not found; grouping is the agent's choice of memory file per topic.

time.fields.t: Only created_at/updated_at system times on every row; no event time, valid time or as-of.

time.update.t: Update = the agent rewrites the whole file in place (last write wins); commit replaces content and re-embeds the description only if it changed. No contradiction detection or history of superseded values.

time.dedup.t: Segment texts deduplicated within a file; unchanged lines keep their embedding (drop-and-add only on the diff); identical texts across a commit share one embedding; resources deduplicated by path. Cross-file duplicate consolidation is an open PR (#708).

derive.profile.t: No dedicated profile object and nothing always-injected; user facts live in agent-curated memory files retrieved like any other. (v1 experiment kept one <name>_profile.txt per speaker, rewritten each session and injected whole with use_profile=prompt.)

derive.entity.t: not found (files are topic-named by the agent, not per entity).

derive.background.t: The whole write path is a background job: the host agent runs headless every 60 min (default) to do leftovers -> prepare -> jobs -> commit; skill extraction ('self-evolve') runs in the same pass. Codex, Cola, OpenClaw and WorkBuddy use their own native schedulers; Claude Code, Cursor, Hermes and pi use the OS (a Windows helper registers a windowless S4U Task Scheduler task; Unix cron/launchd is set up from the host guide).

derive.forget.t: No decay or TTL; deletions of mirrored files are ignored by commit ('Deletions are intentionally not returned'), so the store only grows or is patched.

index.embed.t: OpenAI text-embedding-3-small by default; other providers with their own defaults: jina (jina-embeddings-v3), voyage (voyage-3.5), doubao (doubao-embedding-large-text-250515), openrouter; batch size 64 per request.

index.lexical.t: None at HEAD although ADR 0007 specifies cosine + BM25 hybrid; grep finds no BM25/FTS in src. (v1 experiment had BM25 + string match.)
index.lexical.e: read: src/memu/app/agentic.py:232-264, src/memu/vector.py; doc: docs/adr/0007-three-independent-memory-lines-wiki-graph.md:133-137; read: memU-experiment response_agent.py:341

index.vector.t: Brute-force numpy cosine (argpartition top-k, empty or wrong-dimension vectors skipped) for inmemory and SQLite; SQLite re-reads every scoped segment row by SQL on each retrieve and also appends them to an in-process list with a linear membership check (the quadratic cost open PR #716 targets). Postgres segments use pgvector cosine ORDER BY ... LIMIT with no HNSW/IVF index in the migration; Postgres resources are still scanned in Python.

read.rewrite.t: No engine rewrite; the standing instruction tells the host agent it may reword the user's request 'into a clearer query or focused keywords'.

read.analysis.t: None in HEAD (v1.2.0 had an LLM RETRIEVE/NO_RETRIEVE intention router and per-tier sufficiency checks).
read.analysis.e: read: src/memu/app/settings.py:89-95 (ProgressiveRetrieveConfig docstring); memU v1.2.0 src/memu/app/settings.py:148-163

read.legs.t: Two cosine legs from one query embedding: segments (top 5; the config field file.top_k is described as a file count but bounds segments, see open PR #707) rolled up to their files (file score = max segment score, only hit files fetched via id__in), and workspace-track resources (top 5 captions).

rank.fusion.t: No fusion; separate ranked lists per layer, files ranked by max child segment score.

rank.rerank.t: None at HEAD; an opt-in 'Jev memory reranking' is an open PR (#704).

rank.gate.t: No similarity floor: cosine top-k is always returned; the agent is told to proceed normally if nothing is relevant.

rank.agentic.t: Progressive disclosure for the host agent: segments first, then file summaries with an on-disk path to open only if needed, then resource paths; the agent decides what to read. Engine stays single-shot.

answer.shape.t: JSON printed to the agent's tool output: segments {text, score, source_file}, files {name, track, description, score, path} with content stripped and mirrored to ~/.memu/<track>/<name>.md, resources {path, caption, score}.

answer.size.t: Not measured. Bounded by 5 single-line segments + up to 5 file descriptions + 5 resource captions (file bodies are not inline), roughly hundreds to ~1-2k tokens before any file the agent chooses to open (inferred). v1 experiment: logged retrieved events averaged 10,969 chars per question over 1,540 q, plus a profile file of about 2.7k chars (about 3.4k tokens total, inferred at 4 chars/token).
answer.size.e: inferred from src/memu/app/settings.py:75-95; read: memU-experiment result.json detailed_results (measured), memory/*_profile.txt (53,127 chars / 20 files)

answer.prompt.t: No answer prompt: the host agent answers with its own model; memU only injects a standing 'retrieve before answering' block or skill into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/SOUL.md. (v1 experiment: <thinking>/<result> prompt, answer of at most 20 words, told to resolve relative times.)

eval.best.t: 92.09 on LoCoMo (1,420/1,542) from the v1 experiment repo; no published number for the v2 HEAD engine.
eval.best.e: read: memU-experiment result.json; doc: memU v1.2.0 README.md:331

eval.outside.t: No independent run: absent from OmniMemEval, JustMem and T-Mem; HEAD README dropped the claim.

eval.models.t: Reader gpt-4.1-mini (Azure), judge gpt-4.1 (hard-coded), memory build model unrecorded (store dir name suggests 4.1, inferred).

eval.rigour.t: Single vendor run; whole speaker profile injected into every answer; cat 5 effectively excluded (2 of 446 counted); judge is a stronger model than the reader with lenient yes/no; summary.total_questions=1986 reported beside accuracy computed on 1,542.
eval.rigour.e: read: memU-experiment result.json summary, locomo_test.py:610-632, response_agent.py:803-808

cost.write.t: Engine: 0 LLM calls; all embeddings of a commit go through one embed() call (sequential 64-text requests), skipping unchanged lines and descriptions. Agent-side: 2 agentic jobs per session (memory + skill) plus 1 resource job per run of up to 10 sessions, so for 272 sessions about 544 agent jobs over at least 28 runs (inferred; not measured, multi-call each). v1 experiment: per session per speaker 2-6 extraction/completeness calls + 1 profile rewrite, i.e. about 1,632-3,808 calls for LoCoMo (read).

cost.read.t: 1 embedding call + store scans; 0 LLM calls in the engine (the host agent's own turn pays for reading). v1 experiment: 2-6 LLM calls per question (1-3 sufficiency checks, 0-2 query rewrites, 1 answer) with top-k 25/15/15 events.

cost.where.t: Embeddings hosted (OpenAI default) or any OpenAI-compatible base URL; distillation runs on the user's host agent subscription; optional hosted memory at api.memu.so/api/v4/memory/.

trust.provenance.t: RecallFiles carry no link to the sessions or turns that produced them; resources are paths only. ADR 0006 records the missing skill provenance as an open issue.

trust.erasure.t: No record-level delete in the backend protocol (list/retrieve/commit only) and file deletions are not propagated; erasure is whole-store removal on explicit request during uninstall.

trust.auth.t: Local mode has none (file/DSN access); cloud mode uses a Bearer project API key with authentication/authorisation errors.

trust.sharing.t: Cross-agent by design: every host adapter shares one backend via ~/.memu/config.env, so what one agent's sessions taught is retrieved by another; no per-agent permissions.

extras.t: A second job per session reads messages plus tool calls and creates or branches reusable skill markdown; each skill is embedded as a single 'name: description' segment and retrieved alongside memory.

Files the agent created or edited in a session are logged by the skill job, verified (existing files only, deduped, max 50), described by the agent (or 'null') and embedded by caption for recall as paths. The verifier keeps only paths starting with '/' or '~', so Windows drive-letter paths would be dropped (inferred, not run).
Write-time intelligence is outsourced to the user's own coding agent via self-contained job files; the engine is deterministic prepare/commit with content-hash diffing of the mirrored markdown.

Memory, skill, resource job templates and the retrieval skill are fetched from memu.pro at each prepare (fallback last-good cache then embedded); the vendor can change extraction behaviour without a release. Disable with MEMU_TEMPLATE_BASE_URL empty.
On hosts with skills, the per-turn instruction shrinks to two sentences pointing at a memu-retrieve skill, keeping standing prompt tokens low.

v1 had five memory types (profile, event, knowledge, behavior, skill), ten fixed categories with LLM-rewritten category summaries, a dedup step that was a placeholder, and RAG or LLM retrieval with an intention router and sufficiency checks.
extras.e: read: memU v1.2.0 src/memu/database/models.py:10, src/memu/app/settings.py:74-89, :148-163, src/memu/app/memorize.py:229-230

extras.t: The LoCoMo experiment used per-speaker files: <name>_events.txt (date-prefixed event paragraphs, about 517 chars each) appended per session after an extract/completeness/refine loop, and <name>_profile.txt rewritten per session; read used 0.3 string + 0.3 BM25 + 2.0 cosine weighted scores and an iterative sufficiency loop.

On by default: retrieve, list and commit record counts, outcome and latency (never query text, memory, names or paths; enforced by a property allowlist) to api.memu.so; retrieve POSTs only its own event inline, while the spool (up to 200 POSTs) is flushed by prepare/commit. Off with MEMU_TELEMETRY=0, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or an empty MEMU_EVENTS_BASE_URL.

The retrieve instruction is written between memU begin/end markers in the host's instruction file, replaced in place on upgrade, the old file backed up to .bak, legacy default paths unpatched after install, and the skill installed before the pointer so no instruction ever names a missing skill.

The schedule helper writes the long pipeline prompt to a file and registers a PowerShell wrapper in a memU task folder as an S4U task: windowless, runs while logged out, catches up missed runs, ignores overlapping starts, 10-year repetition so it does not silently stop after a day.

'memu memorize prepare' takes 1-10 strict, versioned MemorizeInput JSON sessions (schema_version 1.0; message, tool_call, tool_result items); memory jobs see only messages, skill jobs see everything; one active run per workspace.

'memu-agent detect' probes an unknown agent: sniffs known JSONL transcript dialects to decide if memorisation works, and looks for AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md / SOUL.md to decide if retrieval can be injected; read-only.

OpenClaw (per-agent SQLite plus legacy JSONL, merged newest-first, generation-aware cursor) and Hermes (state.db) transcripts are read read-only; Claude Code subagent transcripts are attributed to their owning session; Cowork audit logs are a separate source in the Claude Code bridge.
list_all_recall_files returns pages of 50 ordered by (track, name, id) with an opaque base64 cursor; prepare writes each page to disk as it arrives so the whole store is never held in memory.

extras.param: atomic mirror writes on the hot path
extras.t: Mirror files are written to a unique temp file and swapped in with os.replace, because the per-turn retrieve hook rewrites them while agents may be reading.

One retry policy for cloud and embedding clients (408/429/5xx, Retry-After honoured up to 30 s, else 0.25-2 s backoff); loopback endpoints bypass forced proxies in sandboxed hosts; urllib call sites fall back to certifi only when no system CA store exists.
'<binary> doctor' checks that MEMU_* config resolves and that the selected local or cloud backend answers the same retrieval path the host uses, with proxy hints on transport failures.

token_economy.t: Three mechanisms: (1) zero LLM tokens in the engine on both paths, the only model cost is embeddings, all sent through one embed() call per commit (64 texts per request) and skipped for unchanged lines/descriptions; (2) progressive disclosure at read: 5 one-line segments + file descriptions with paths instead of bodies, so the agent opens a full file only when a segment is too thin; (3) a two-sentence standing instruction pointing at a skill on hosts that support skills. Write-side distillation is cheap for the engine but not free: it spends the host agent's tokens on 2 jobs per session, and jobs read file names before bodies to limit that. No context budget, compression model or summarisation is enforced; per-question context is not measured. v1 experiment by contrast spent about 3.4k tokens of context per question (inferred) plus up to 6 LLM calls.

speed.t: Read: one embedding call then brute-force cosine (numpy argpartition) or a pgvector ORDER BY without an ANN index; resource leg lists the full scoped resource table per query; latency_ms is recorded per retrieve but no figures are published. Write: fully asynchronous to the user (hourly scheduled job), embeddings batched, unchanged segments not re-embedded, one listing per track per commit; up to 10 sessions per run. Open PR #716 removes quadratic SQLite segment-cache scans.
speed.e: read: src/memu/vector.py:23-73, src/memu/app/agentic.py:308-329, :520-533, src/memu/hosts/retrieval.py:156-173, src/memu/hosts/scheduling/windows.py:44; gh pr #716

keep: Plan-embed-write commit: batch every embedding into one call before any write so a failed commit is a no-op and safely retryable.
Line-level segments rolled up to their parent document (file score = max segment score): cheap fine-grained recall with a coarse document for context.
Progressive disclosure at read: return short slices plus descriptions and paths, let the reader open full documents only on demand.
Diff-based re-embedding: hash content, re-embed only changed lines and changed descriptions.
Cursor staged at prepare and promoted only on commit, so a crashed background pass re-offers work instead of losing it.
avoid: No relevance floor and no lexical leg at HEAD (ADR promises BM25 hybrid, code is cosine top-5 only), so off-topic queries always return memory.
No provenance, no record deletion and ignored file deletions: memory grows monotonically and cannot be traced or erased per item.
Extraction quality, dates and contradictions depend entirely on the host agent and on prompt templates fetched live from the vendor's server; timestamps are stripped before extraction.
The headline LoCoMo 92.09 is a v1, vendor-run, profile-injected, cat-5-excluded number with a stronger judge, and does not describe the current engine.
in_progress: No commits since the pinned dc7bda8 (upstream HEAD is still dc7bda8 on 2026-10-11, a dependency CVE bump); the last feature merges were #695 batch developer memorize sessions, #694 hit-only file roll-up, #693 skip empty or wrong-dimension vectors and #675 pi adapter (gh api commits).

specialities.name: Host agent as the extractor
specialities.t: The engine makes no LLM calls at all; write-time distillation is handed to the user's own coding agent through self-contained job files (read transcript, read file names first, no-op/patch/create), and the engine only diffs and embeds what the agent left on disk.

specialities.name: Plan-embed-write commit with embedding tickets
specialities.t: Commit plans every write first, registers each text for a vector ticket (identical texts share one), resolves all vectors in one embed call, then writes; a provider failure writes nothing, and unchanged lines and descriptions keep their stored vectors.

specialities.name: Crash-safe staged cursor and hash-diff commit
specialities.t: prepare stages the advanced session cursor in a .pending file and commit promotes it only after the store accepts; changed files are found by SHA-256 against a snapshot re-taken only on successful commit, so a crashed run is re-offered rather than lost (#518).

specialities.name: Self-session exclusion by exact identity
specialities.t: The scheduled bridging run is itself a host session; it is recognised by a launch environment marker plus the host's session-id variable, never by matching transcript content, so memU does not mine its own bookkeeping (#606, ADR 0015).

specialities.name: Progressive disclosure with skill-split standing prompt
specialities.t: Retrieve returns one-line segments, then file descriptions with an on-disk path instead of bodies, then resource paths; on hosts with skills the always-loaded instruction shrinks to two sentences and the full procedure lives in a skill read only when retrieving.

specialities.name: Line segments rolled up to documents
specialities.t: Every non-blank, non-heading line of a memory file is its own embedded segment, and hits roll up to the parent file with score = max segment score, giving fine-grained recall plus a coarse document without a second search.

specialities.name: Server-refreshable prompts with contract checks
specialities.t: Job templates and the retrieval skill are pulled from the vendor server (4 s timeout, 64 KB cap) and used only if they keep their placeholder contract and format cleanly; otherwise last-good cache, then embedded copy. Never downgrades an installed skill on outage.

specialities.name: Skill track as procedural memory
specialities.t: A second job per session mines messages plus tool calls into reusable skill markdown, told to branch an existing skill ('case X, do ...') rather than spawn near-duplicates; each skill is indexed as one name+description segment.
